root_cause.text: smb2_open in the ksmbd durable-handle reconnect path releases the durable file descriptor reference with ksmbd_put_durable_fd() before all later uses of dh_info.fp/fp are finished, allowing the ksmbd_file object to be freed and then accessed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes multiple early ksmbd_put_durable_fd(dh_info.fp)/ksmbd_put_durable_fd(fp) calls from the durable reconnect branch, adds a single put only at the end of smb2_open when dh_info.reconnected is true, and the CVE/commit text explicitly states that the early put could lead to use-after-free on later accesses such as fp->create_time if a subsequent error or scavenger action occurred.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove premature durable-fd releases in smb2_open() reconnect handling to preserve correct file handle lifetime on success and error paths.
intent_record.what: The change removes four calls to ksmbd_put_durable_fd() from the durable-handle reconnect path in smb2_open(): two immediately before goto err_out2 after smb2_check_durable_oplock() and ksmbd_reopen_durable_fd() failures, one before goto err_out2 when ksmbd_override_fsids() fails, and one unconditionally after ksmbd_vfs_getattr(&fp->filp->f_path, &stat).
intent_record.how: At runtime, the durable file descriptor is no longer released at those intermediate points, avoiding an extra or premature reference drop during reconnect/open handling and leaving cleanup to the common error path or later logic. This prevents incorrect lifetime management of the durable handle, especially on failure paths and before subsequent use of fp.

intent_record.intent_summary: Release the durable file reference on reconnected handles in smb2_open() to avoid leaking the durable fd during reconnect processing.
intent_record.what: A new conditional block was added before freeing local resources in smb2_open(): if dh_info.reconnected is true, ksmbd_put_durable_fd(dh_info.fp) is called.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when an open request involves a reconnected durable handle, the associated durable file pointer now has its reference released before function exit, preventing the reconnected file descriptor from being left retained after smb2_open() completes.

The change directly modifies when smb2_open() releases the durable file reference in the reconnect path, which is the same reference-lifetime issue at the heart of the vulnerability. Even if intended to fix a leak, it affects the ksmbd_put_durable_fd() timing that caused use-after-free of dh_info.fp/fp.

In the reconnect path, this releases the durable handle reference before all subsequent uses of dh_info.fp/fp are complete; if execution later accesses the same object, it may have already been freed.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement drops the durable file reference in smb2_open() reconnect handling before later code finishes using fp/dh_info.fp. That premature release can free the underlying ksmbd_file object and lead to a use-after-free on subsequent accesses.

This statement releases the durable handle reference too early in the reconnect path. Later logic still depends on dh_info.fp/fp remaining valid, so the object may be freed and then reused, matching the root-cause use-after-free.

In this commit version, the code does `rc = ksmbd_vfs_getattr(&fp->filp->f_path, &stat);` and then immediately `ksmbd_put_durable_fd(fp);` before `if (rc) goto err_out2;` and before `goto reconnected_fp;`. The stated root cause is releasing the durable file reference before all later uses of `dh_info.fp/fp` are finished, allowing the `ksmbd_file` to be freed and later accessed. That vulnerable construct is present here because the reference is dropped prior to the later control flow into `reconnected_fp`, meaning the function can continue after `ksmbd_put_durable_fd(fp)` and potentially use `fp` after release. This commit only fixes a refcount leak on the error path from `ksmbd_vfs_getattr()` by moving `ksmbd_put_durable_fd(fp)` before the `if (rc)` check; it does not introduce the correct handling for the use-after-free root cause. Therefore the bug is present and the fix for this vulnerability is not yet in this function.
